value.finding: The guide prints the exact route key and describes the right Connecticut mechanism - physical destruction under C.G.S. Sec. 54-142a(g)(1) of records already erased, distinguished from erasure itself. The route-obligation census pinned by this very packet (data/rcap-grade-a/route-obligation-census-candidate/route-obligation-candidate.json, f6fc0814..., which the receipt hashes and which recomputes equal here) records currentOutputStrategy 'participant_agency_application' for this route and a participantFacingInstrument that is an application or written request, not a guide. The delivered artifact is an agency_preparation_guide whose own first lines read 'THIS IS AN AGENCY-APPLICATION PREPARATION GUIDE, NOT AN OFFICIAL FORM AND NOT A COURT FILING', and whose source-receipt.json states 'The output is a preparation guide and not a written destruction request.' A guide cannot replace an owed application or request. This is not a build defect and not repairable inside the directory: CT.memo.json authorises process_guidance for this track precisely because no accepted request format has been confirmed, and the census's own missingImplementationWork begins 'Acquire and verify exact official-source'. It is an owner and source question about what this route delivers, which is why the verdict is PRODUCT_PATH_PENDING rather than FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED.

The single declared component, agency_preparation_guide, is present and complete in both fixtures, and CT.memo.json names exactly one component for this track with role process_guidance and requirement required, so against the memo the component set is whole. Against the census route contract it is not: the route's participant-facing instrument is a request to the clerk, the field map classifies the sole component's documentRole as 'instructions', and the guide expressly disclaims being the request. Held open on that contradiction rather than passed.
